claims_checked.claim: schema/config.schema.json:523 — the finding_cap description for instruments.audit-changes: "the budget one audit lane reports under, counted in CLASSES: an unjustified edit pattern recurring across hunks is ONE concern whose locations name every hunk (RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP), so a class spanning forty hunks costs one."
claims_checked.evidence: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:720 sets a["finding_cap"] = get(cfg["instruments"]["audit-changes"], "finding_cap", 8), passed into the lane brief; RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP (policy.md) is exactly the class-not-site counting rule described, and finding.schema.json's unbounded `locations` array is how one class names every hunk.

claims_checked.claim: schema/exemptions.schema.json:62 — the reason field's description: "a loose floor here on purpose: the schema refuses only a reason that is no reason at all, and CFG.EXEMPTIONS checks the real bound of 40 characters per entry. Raising this one crashes Ledger.read, and with it sync, every scan and the docs build, where the doctor would have named the entry and carried on."
claims_checked.evidence: schema minLength is 24 (the loose floor); src/CLI/Doctor.jl:331 enforces length(e["reason"]) >= 40 inside CFG.EXEMPTIONS (a doctor finding, not a throw). src/CLI/Ledger.jl:38-39 validates against the schema and throws LedgerError on any violation, and Ledger.read is used by Config, Sync, the scans and Doctor itself — so raising minLength to 40 in the schema would turn a 24-39 char reason into a hard throw at every one of those call sites, exactly as described.

claims_checked.claim: schema/hat.schema.json:37 — the substrate field's description: "the corpus the hat works in. TWO values, because the panel splits the manuscript once: what ELSE a hat is handed is needs, not a substrate value."
claims_checked.evidence: hat.schema.json's substrate enum is exactly ["full", "siteonly"] (two values); needs is a separate sibling array property, carried through unchanged into rendered args at src/CLI/Preflight.jl:701, confirming the two are distinct, separately-plumbed fields.

findings.title: config.schema.json permits two consumer knobs no engine ever reads
findings.description: Both fields validate, both get an initial value written by gbg init (src/CLI/Init.jl:149-163), and both are documented in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as real per-package settings (ARCHITECTURE.md:1241,1353,1418,2145 for latex_source_globs), but neither is read by any engine, scan, doctor check, or Workflow-args builder. docs.doctest appears nowhere outside schema/config.schema.json and Init.jl; ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl's makedocs wrapper forwards only the consumer's own kwargs... straight to Documenter.makedocs, never consulting cfg["docs"]["doctest"]. latex_source_globs is likewise absent from every .jl file except Init.jl's default-writer — Preflight.jl's render_args check-consistency branch (lines 697-703) has no such field, and no catalog/ or instruments/*/workflow/*.js file reads it either. A schema that admits and documents a field nobody consumes misdescribes the tool's actual configurable surface.
findings.resolution_hint: Either wire docs.doctest into the makedocs wrapper (pass it as the doctest kwarg unless the consumer's own docs/make.jl overrides it) and wire latex_source_globs into whatever latex-notation scan or hat substrate it was designed for, or drop both keys from config.schema.json (and Init.jl's generated default) and record the removal as a MAJOR per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5.5's closed-vocabulary rule.
